original_value: In this article, a class of mean-field-type games with discrete-continuous state spaces is considered. We establish Bellman systems which provide sufficiency conditions for mean-field-type equilibria in state-and-mean-field-type feedback form. We then derive unnormalized master adjoint systems (MASS). The methodology is shown to be flexible enough to capture multi-class interaction in epidemic propagation in which multiple authorities are risk-aware atomic decision-makers and individuals are risk-aware non-atomic decision-makers. Based on MASS, we present a data-driven modelling and analytics for mitigating Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). The model integrates untested cases, age-structure, decision-making, gender, pre-existing health conditions, location, testing capacity, hospital capacity, and a mobility map of local areas, including in-cities, inter-cities, and internationally. It is shown that the data-driven model can capture most of the reported data on COVID-19 on confirmed cases, deaths, recovered, number of testing and number of active cases in 66+ countries. The model also reports non-Gaussian and non-exponential properties in 15+ countries.

result.paraphrase: This article studies a class of mean-field-type games with discrete-continuous state spaces. We derive Bellman systems that give sufficient conditions for mean-field-type equilibria in state-and-mean-field-type feedback form, followed by unnormalized master adjoint systems (MASS). The approach is flexible enough to represent multi-class interaction in epidemic spread, where several authorities are risk-aware atomic decision-makers and individuals are risk-aware non-atomic decision-makers. Using MASS, we develop a data-driven model and analytics framework for mitigating Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). The model incorporates untested cases, age structure, decision-making, gender, pre-existing health conditions, location, testing capacity, hospital capacity, and a mobility map of local areas, including in-cities, inter-cities, and international travel. It is shown to capture most reported COVID-19 data on confirmed cases, deaths, recoveries, testing numbers, and active cases across 66+ countries. The model also exhibits non-Gaussian and non-exponential properties in 15+ countries.
